<!--
A persona is a research synthesis, not a character sketch. `/brainstorm` offers
personas at the `standard` and `full` tiers and has `ux-researcher` write them to
`design/product/personas/<slug>.md` (slug = kebab-case of the persona name). PRDs
cite a persona in their `## User Value` section; usability studies recruit against
the segment line above.

Rules:
- Every statement traces to evidence listed under `## Evidence` (participant IDs,
  survey question, analytics query). A statement with no evidence is labelled
  `Hypothesis:` until a study confirms it.
- Behaviour and context over demographics. Age, job and city matter only when they
  change what the person needs or can do.
- Participant IDs (P1, P2, …), never names or contact details. No photos of real
  people.
- Small qualitative samples do not estimate proportions: write "5 of 7
  participants", never "70% of users".

MACHINE CONTRACT — keep the six `##` headings below exactly as spelled, in this
order. Write the body in the team's language.

Examples use Moa, a B2C subscription savings app for the Korean market; the persona
and findings are illustrative. Delete these comments when the persona is written.
-->

## Role & Context

[Who this person is in relation to the problem: life or work situation, the moment
the problem shows up, the devices and channels they use, constraints (time, money,
permissions, accessibility needs).]

*Example (Moa — "Payday Saver")*: Salaried, late 20s, paid on the 25th; banks with a
main bank app plus a super-app; checks balances on the commute; has tried an
installment savings product and a savings memo in a notes app.

## Jobs-to-be-Done

| Job statement ("When …, I want to …, so I can …") | Type (functional / emotional / social) | Importance | Current satisfaction |
|---|---|---|---|
| [When my salary arrives, I want part of it set aside before I spend it, so I can reach my goal without relying on willpower] | functional | high | low |
| [When I look at my goal, I want to see steady progress, so I can feel in control of my money] | emotional | [...] | [...] |

## Goals & Pains

- **Goals**: [the outcomes this person is trying to reach — e.g. a trip fund by
  next summer, a three-month emergency fund]
- **Pains**: [what gets in the way or hurts today — e.g. forgetting the payday
  transfer, the penalty for breaking an installment savings product early]
- **Anxieties about a new solution**: [e.g. an app debiting the salary account
  automatically; not being able to stop it]

## Current Alternatives

| Alternative | Why they use it | Where it fails them |
|---|---|---|
| [installment savings product at their main bank] | [discipline, interest] | [rigid, one goal per product, penalty to break] |
| [manual transfer on payday] | [free, flexible] | [skipped when a month is tight] |

## Decision Criteria

[What this person weighs when choosing and paying — ranked. Include switching
costs and trust signals.]

1. [Safety of money — who holds it, whether it is protected]
2. [Control — can pause, resize or stop anytime]
3. [Effort — sign-up in minutes, sign-in with an account they already have]
4. [Price — free to start; would pay for [...] only if [...]]
